site.name: forge-coder
site.summary: Forge Coder — agentic coding IDE (local demo) Fictional agentic coding product. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Agent run view Three-pane IDE-style layout: file tree (left) + agent chat (center) + live diff preview (right). Left — file tree: - Virtual TypeScript project (`atlas-cli`) with folder collapse, file-status badges (M for modified, + for newly added), and a summary footer. - Clicking any file marked M / + loads its diff into the right pane.

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the Forge Coder agentic IDE interface, validating the primary agent chat flow, file tree interactions, diff preview states, and responsive layout behavior.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed by first validating the primary agent run view and its interactive states (interrupt, rerun, chat). Next, it will deep-dive into the file tree and diff preview pane interactions, including view toggles and file selection. It will then test the top-level navigation tabs and header actions. Finally, the entire critical flow will be validated on a mobile viewport to assess responsive layout and tap target issues identified in the prescan.
assumptions: The application is a single-page local demo where navigation tabs (Agent, Inbox, Runs, Settings) may dynamically swap content or are placeholder controls.
Clicking files marked with 'M' or '+' in the file tree will update the right diff pane, while unmarked files may not.
The 'Interrupt' and 'Rerun' buttons will alter the agent's state visually in the UI, even if no real backend exists.
The 'Auto-apply edits' checkbox and chat input are functional UI controls that change the application's visual state.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets on mobile for file tree icons (⌕, +) and the 'Auto-apply edits' checkbox (13x13px)
Top navigation tabs (Agent, Inbox, Runs, Settings) which are small (50-70x32px) and may cause layout or interaction issues on mobile
State transition when 'Interrupt' or 'Rerun' is clicked—potential for broken or stalled UI states
Three-pane layout collapse behavior on mobile viewports

phases.title: Agent Run State & Chat Controls
phases.objective: Validate the primary agent run view, state transitions, and chat input functionality.
key_checks: Click '⏸ Interrupt' and verify the agent status updates appropriately
Click '↻ Rerun' and verify the run resets or restarts visually
Type a message in the 'Reply...' textarea and click 'Send'
Toggle the 'Auto-apply edits' checkbox on and off
exit_criteria: Agent state controls have been exercised
Chat input and submission work without errors

phases.title: File Tree & Diff Preview Interactions
phases.objective: Validate file tree navigation, folder collapse, file status badges, and the resulting diff preview updates.
key_checks: Click a folder (e.g., 'src' or 'upload') to collapse and expand it
Click a file marked 'M' (e.g., 'stream.ts') and verify the diff loads in the right pane
Click a file marked '+' (e.g., 'index.ts') and verify the diff loads
Click an unmarked file (e.g., 'retry.ts') and observe the right pane behavior
Click 'Accept all changes' and 'Open editor' buttons
exit_criteria: File tree interactions correctly update the diff pane
Diff view toggles function as expected
Diff action buttons have been clicked and observed

phases.title: Top Navigation & Header Actions
phases.objective: Validate the behavior of top-level tabs and header buttons.
key_checks: Click 'Inbox', 'Runs', and 'Settings' tabs to check for view changes or UI feedback
Click 'Agent' tab to return to the main view
exit_criteria: All top navigation tabs have been clicked
Header action buttons have been exercised

phases.title: Mobile Responsive Validation
phases.objective: Validate the layout, readability, and tap-target usability on a mobile viewport.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and verify the three-pane layout adapts correctly (e.g., panes stack or collapse)
Check if file tree and diff pane are accessible on mobile
Attempt to tap small controls identified in prescan (Auto-apply checkbox, nav tabs, tree icons)
Test chat input and send functionality on mobile
exit_criteria: Mobile layout has been assessed for major usability flaws
Small tap target warnings have been visually confirmed
Core agent flow is functional on mobile

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all 11 buttons, 4 links, 2 inputs, and key file tree interactions
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical agent, file tree, and diff checks on mobile viewport to validate layout and tap targets

notes: Prescan flagged 12 small tap target warnings, predominantly affecting the header nav, file tree icons, and the auto-apply checkbox; pay special attention to these during the mobile phase.
Since this is a local demo, 'Connect a repo' and 'Open in VS Code' may trigger external protocol handlers or simply fail gracefully; observe the UI reaction.

observation.visible_text: Forge / atlas-cli ⌥ feat/streaming-uploads Agent Inbox Runs Settings Connect a repo Open in VS Code RT ATLAS-CLI ⌕ + src upload › stream.ts M › chunker.ts M › retry.ts › index.ts + commands core main.ts test upload.spec.ts M retry.spec.ts auth.spec.ts docs package.json tsconfig.json README.md Modified 3 Added 1 Lines changed +128 / -54 Run #243 · paused · 4m 12s elapsed ⏸ Interrupt ↻ Rerun Streaming multipart uploads keep failing on slow connections. Resumes after a network drop just re-upload the whole file. Implement chunked resumable uploads (5 MiB chunks), persist progress to .forge/state.json, and write tests. Don't touch the auth flow. FC I scoped the work to src/upload/ and skimmed the existing stream module. Plan: Split stream.ts: extract a new chunker.ts for chunk-boundary logic (pure functions, easy to test). Add a ChunkedUpload class in index.ts that consults .forge/state.json on start and writes after each chunk. Wire backoff using the existing retry.ts — it already has the right shape. Write tests in test/upload.spec.ts covering: fresh upload, resume mid-stream, retry on 5xx, abort on 4xx. Continuing. 📖 Reading src/upload/stream.ts 208 lines · stable interface 3m 58s ago 📖 Reading src/upload/retry.ts and test/retry.spec.ts retry exponent base = 2, jitter ≤ 250ms — fine to reuse 3m 41s ago ✎ Edited src/upload/stream.ts −47 / +12 — extracted chunker 2m 58s ago ✎ Created src/upload/chunker.ts +86 — pure chunk-boundary helpers 2m 31s ago ✎ Created src/upload/index.ts (ChunkedUpload class) +184 — start/resume/abort lifecycle, persists to .forge/state.json 1m 49s ago ✎ Edited test/upload.spec.ts +102 — four new cases 1m 09s ago ▶ Running pnpm test test/upload.spec.ts 6 of 8 cases · fresh-upload passed 27s ⏸ Interrupted by user Run paused. Send a message to redirect, or click Rerun to retry. just now Suggest, then ask the agent to apply: Auto-apply edits Send src/upload/chunker.ts +86 / −0 Open editor Accept all changes Unified Split @@ -0,0 +1,86 @@ src/upload/chunker.ts + import { Readable } from "stream"; + + export const DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024; + + export interface Chunk { + index: number; + start: number; + end: number; // exclusive + etag?: string; + uploaded?: boolean; + } + + export function planChunks(byteLength: number, chunkSize = DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE): Chunk[] { + if (byteLength <= 0) return []; + const out: Chunk[] = []; + let i = 0, offset = 0; + while (offset < byteLength) { + const end = Math.min(byteLength, offset + chunkSize); + out.push({ index: i, start: offset, end }); + offset = end; i++; + } + return out; + } + + export function mergeProgress(plan: Chunk[], known: Chunk[]): Chunk[] { + const map = new Map(known.map(k => [k.index, k])); + return plan.map(p => ({ ...p, ...(map.get(p.index) ?? {}) })); + } + + export function nextChunk(plan: Chunk[]): Chunk | null { + for (const c of plan) if (!c.uploaded) return c; + return null; + } + + export async function* sliceReadable(src: Readable, plan: Chunk[]) { + const buf: Buffer[] = []; + let bytesQueued = 0; + let cursor = 0; + for await (const piece of src) { + buf.push(piece); + bytesQueued += piece.length; + while (cursor < plan.length && bytesQueued >= plan[cursor].end) { + const need = plan[cursor].end - plan[cursor].start; + const joined = Buffer.concat(buf, bytesQueued); + yield { chunk: plan[cursor], body: joined.subarray(plan[cursor].start, plan[cursor].end) }; + cursor++; + } + } + } ✓ Type-checked clean (tsc) ✓ ESLint — no new warnings ▶ Tests: 6 / 8 — run in progress

Resumes after a network drop just re-upload the whole file. Implement chunked resumable uploads (5 MiB chunks), persist progress to .forge/state.json, and write tests. Don't touch the auth flow. FC I scoped the work to src/upload/ and skimmed the existing stream module. Plan: Split stream.ts: extract a new chunker.ts for chunk-boundary logic (pure functions, easy to test). Add a ChunkedUpload class in index.ts that consults .forge/state.json on start and writes after each chunk. Wire backoff using the existing retry.ts — it already has the right shape. Write tests in test/upload.spec.ts covering: fresh upload, resume mid-stream, retry on 5xx, abort on 4xx.
